title: Introduce contextualized log-strips and token-surge guard for quieter alerts
author: Jordan Patel
release_notes: Adds a lightweight sampled-log visualization ('log-strips') for long-tail traces and a token-surge guard alert to reduce noisy SRE alerts during transient token bursts.
description: Motivation: noisy alerting from short-lived token/spike bursts and overly verbose log samples make SRE triage slow. This PR introduces 'log-strips' (a lightweight, time-aligned sampled-log strip per invocation) to surface the most relevant log slices alongside invocation traces, and a Token-Surge Guard alert rule that attenuates alerting for short-duration token spikes while preserving real SLO breaches. What changed: 1) observability/log_strip: new collector that attaches N compact log snippets per invocation keyed by phase (init, prompt, generation, commit) with de-duplication heuristics and context anchors; 2) renderer: a minimal React panel used in dashboards to render aligned log strips with hover-to-expand; 3) token_surge_guard.yaml: an alert rule that computes burst windows and applies adaptive quieting thresholds before firing PagerDuty alerts; 4) registry: added opt-in sampling registration so teams can enable log-strips per-tenant; 5) dashboards: a new 'Log Strips' panel + integrated example on invocation detail dashboard; 6) docs and tests. Design notes: log-strips are stored as ephemeral attachments to sampled traces (TTL 24h) and indexed by invocation_id and token_phase to keep cardinality low. The guard uses a sliding-window burst detector (configurable window=30s, cooloff=2min, min_tokens=500) and ties into existing alert dedupers to avoid silencing legitimate prolonged degradations. Important trade-offs and mitigations: we keep stored snippet lengths capped and run a token-cost estimation to avoid unexpected storage bloat; snippet retention and sampling rate are configurable per-tenant. Checklist: [x] Collector implementation and unit tests; [x] Dashboard panel and renderer; [x] Alert rule with integration E2E; [x] Docs and rollout guide; [x] Feature flag gating (off by default - opt-in per-tenant). Commits summary: - Add log-strip collector and sampling registry (Jordan Patel) - Add dashboard panel and renderer with small CSS optimizations (Design: Miles Ortega) - Add token-surge guard alert rule + e2e test harness (Chen Li) - Docs and runbook (Jordan Patel) Files changed (high level snippets): observability/log_strip/collector.go - implemented ring buffer per-invocation and phase tagging (approx 220 LOC); infra/alerts/token_surge_guard.yaml - new PromQL-based rule that calls burst_detector function and integrates with alertmanager annotations; dashboards/log-strips-panel.json - dashboard spec with panel id, metrics query examples and links to invocation detail. Testing: unit tests added for collector and burst detector (tests/obs/log_strips_test.go). E2E test (tests/alerts/token_surge_guard_e2e.test.ts) simulates token burst traffic and verifies no PD alert during <30s bursts but fires when bursts exceed configured windows. CI: lint and unit tests green, e2e initially flaky on CI cluster (race on test harness); reran the pipeline and passed. Rollout plan: feature-gated rollout in three stages: 1) internal dogfooding org (1 week), 2) opt-in beta tenants (2 weeks), 3) gradual auto-sample enable for high-volume tenants (monitor storage delta, disable if >5% increase). Observability knobs added to console under tenant settings (sampling rate, retention, min_token_threshold). Backwards compatibility: collector attaches to sampled traces only, no change to existing trace schema. Ops notes: if you see an unexpected increase in metric observability.log_strip_stored_bytes, flip sampling_rate back to 0. Reviewers should pay attention to token cost calculation in collector and PromQL correctness in alert rule.
